title: Set up your environment
description: Run a small open-weight model locally and a deterministic fake server, both serving the chat-completions API.
outcome: You can reach a /v1/chat/completions endpoint (real or fake) and verify it from Python.
environment: Python 3.12 (macOS: brew install python@3.12; Windows: winget Python.Python.3.12 + py launcher), requests 2.34.2; fake_model_server.py (stdlib); optional: Ollama 0.40.12 + qwen2.5:1.5b (Q4_K_M, 986 MB; CPU, or GPU via Metal on Apple silicon / CUDA, ROCm or Vulkan on Windows). Full workstation setup: ../shared/WORKSTATION-SETUP.md
overview: Every lab talks to one URL shape: <base>/v1/chat/completions. Use Ollama with a small CPU model, or the stdlib fake server for tests and offline work.
prerequisites: ~2 GB free disk and 4 GB RAM for the optional qwen2.5:1.5b model
Bigger models: size by download (qwen2.5 Q4_K_M: 1.5b 986 MB, 7b 4.7 GB, 14b 9.0 GB, 32b 20 GB) plus context memory; check the real footprint with ollama ps (documentation/HARDWARE.md)

glossary.meaning: HTTP API that accepts the same JSON as POST /v1/chat/completions; many local servers implement it.
Model whose weights you can download and run yourself (here qwen2.5:1.5b, Apache-2.0).
Deterministic program that returns protocol-correct replies so code can be tested without a model.

concepts: One wire format, many servers: switch back ends by changing LOCAL_MODEL_URL and LOCAL_MODEL.
Small quantized models (1-2B, Q4) run on CPU; slower but fine for learning.
Tests should never depend on a live model: use a deterministic stand-in.
Same server on a Mac mini (Metal GPU) or a Windows PC (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm/Vulkan, else CPU); `ollama ps` shows where the model landed.
inRealSystems: Ollama, llama.cpp's llama-server and vLLM all serve /v1/chat/completions, so only LOCAL_MODEL_URL and LOCAL_MODEL change between them.
useWhen: Use for learning, private data and offline CI; not for judging model quality.

"""Check that a chat-completions server is up: list models, then send one chat request.

Real model : LOCAL_MODEL_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 LOCAL_MODEL=qwen2.5:1.5b python check_endpoint.py
Fake model : LOCAL_MODEL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1  LOCAL_MODEL=fake-model   python check_endpoint.py
The older names BASE_URL / MODEL still work as a fallback (LOCAL_MODEL_URL / LOCAL_MODEL win if both are set).
"""
import os
import sys

import requests

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL") or os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL") or os.environ.get("MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")  # one wire format, many servers: only the URL + model name change


def check(base_url=BASE_URL, model=MODEL):
    models = requests.get(f"{base_url}/models", timeout=10)  # health check: what can this server serve?
    models.raise_for_status()
    ids = [m["id"] for m in models.json()["data"]]
    print("models served:", ids)
    if model not in ids:
        print(f"WARNING: {model!r} not listed - pull it first (ollama pull {model})")
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat/completions", timeout=120, json={
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the single word: ready"}],
        "temperature": 0,
    })
    resp.raise_for_status()
    reply = resp.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    print("chat reply:", reply)
    return ids, reply


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        check()
    except requests.ConnectionError:
        sys.exit(f"Cannot reach {BASE_URL} - is the server running?")

"""Call a chat model over plain HTTP (no SDK): POST /v1/chat/completions and read the reply."""
import json
import os

import requests

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL") or os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1")  # Ollama default
MODEL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL") or os.environ.get("MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")


def chat(messages, base_url=BASE_URL, model=MODEL, temperature=0.0, max_tokens=200):
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": messages,          # stateless: the WHOLE {"role", "content"} history, every call
        "temperature": temperature,    # sampling: 0 = most repeatable; higher = more varied
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,      # hard cap on reply length
    }
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=120)
    resp.raise_for_status()            # turn 4xx/5xx into an exception
    return resp.json()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    data = chat([{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one short sentence."}])
    choice = data["choices"][0]
    print("reply        :", choice["message"]["content"])
    print("finish_reason:", choice["finish_reason"])  # "stop" = done, "length" = hit max_tokens
    print("usage        :", json.dumps(data.get("usage")))
    print("top-level keys:", sorted(data))

title: Prompt structure
description: Compare user-only, system+user and few-shot+delimited prompts on the same task.
outcome: You can put rules in the system message, show the output format with examples, and fence input data with delimiters.
environment: Python 3.12 (macOS: brew python@3.12; Windows: python.org installer + py launcher), requests 2.34.2; fake_model_server.py (stdlib); optional: Ollama 0.40.12 + qwen2.5:1.5b (Q4_K_M, 986 MB; CPU, or GPU via Metal on Apple silicon / CUDA, ROCm or Vulkan on Windows)
overview: Where text goes matters: rules in system, data in user, format shown by examples, data fenced by tags.

glossary.meaning: Instructions from the application, placed first; higher priority than user text in most chat templates.
Example user/assistant pairs placed before the real input to show the desired output.
Markers such as <review>...</review> that separate data from instructions.

concepts: The server turns the message list into one token sequence using the model's chat template.
Few-shot examples steer format more reliably than adjectives in instructions.
Delimiters make it clear which text is data; they reduce but do not eliminate prompt injection.
inRealSystems: Hugging Face Transformers ships each model's chat template (apply_chat_template); Ollama, llama.cpp and vLLM apply it server-side.
useWhen: Use when the format must be exact; skip when context is tight or the task is open-ended writing.

"""Same task, three prompt structures: user-only, system+user, system+few-shot+delimited input."""
import os

import requests

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL") or os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL") or os.environ.get("MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")
REVIEW = "The battery died after two days and support never answered my emails."


def chat(messages, base_url=BASE_URL, model=MODEL):
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat/completions", timeout=120,
                         json={"model": model, "messages": messages, "temperature": 0})
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()


# system role: the application's rules, sent first
SYSTEM = ("You are a sentiment classifier for product reviews. "
          "Reply with exactly one word: positive, negative or neutral.")

PROMPTS = {
    # A: everything in one user message -> free-form, chatty answer
    "A user-only": [
        {"role": "user", "content": f"What is the sentiment of this review? {REVIEW}"}],
    # B: rules in the system message, data in the user message
    "B system+user": [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
        {"role": "user", "content": REVIEW}],
    # C: + few-shot examples that fix the output format, + input wrapped in delimiters
    "C few-shot+delimiters": [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM + " Use the exact format shown in the examples. "
                                               "Classify only the text inside <review> tags."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "<review>I love it, setup took two minutes.</review>"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "POSITIVE"},  # few-shot: the model copies this format
        {"role": "user", "content": "<review>Arrived broken, asked for a refund.</review>"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "NEGATIVE"},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"<review>{REVIEW}</review>"}],  # delimiters: data, not instructions
}


def run_all(base_url=BASE_URL, model=MODEL):
    return {name: chat(msgs, base_url, model) for name, msgs in PROMPTS.items()}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, answer in run_all().items():
        print(f"[{name}] -> {answer}")

code:
"""One tool, one round trip: model asks for get_time -> we run it locally -> model answers."""
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import requests

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL") or os.environ.get("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL") or os.environ.get("MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")

TOOLS = [{  # tool declaration: name + description + JSON-schema parameters
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_time",
        "description": "Return the current UTC date and time in ISO 8601 format.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []},
    },
}]


def get_time():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


LOCAL_FUNCTIONS = {"get_time": get_time}  # allow-list: only these names can ever run


def chat(messages, base_url=BASE_URL, model=MODEL):
    resp = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat/completions", timeout=120,
                         json={"model": model, "messages": messages, "tools": TOOLS, "temperature": 0})
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()["choices"][0]["message"]


def run_tool(call):
    fn = LOCAL_FUNCTIONS.get(call["function"]["name"])
    if fn is None:
        return f"error: unknown tool {call['function']['name']!r}"
    raw = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
    args = raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else json.loads(raw)  # /v1 sends a JSON string; some native APIs an object
    return str(fn(**args))


def ask(question, **kw):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]
    reply = chat(messages, **kw)
    calls = reply.get("tool_calls") or []
    if not calls:                      # model answered directly
        return reply["content"]
    messages.append(reply)             # round trip: the assistant turn with tool_calls goes first
    for call in calls:
        print(f"model requested: {call['function']['name']}({call['function']['arguments']})")
        result = run_tool(call)
        print(f"tool result    : {result}")
        messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": result})  # id links result to call
    return chat(messages, **kw)["content"]  # second call: model sees the tool result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("final answer   :", ask("What time is it right now (UTC)?"))

title: A minimal agent loop
description: Loop model -> tool calls -> results -> model with a max-steps budget, a stop condition and step logs.
outcome: You can write and reason about an agent loop in ~40 lines without a framework.
environment: Python 3.12 (macOS: brew python@3.12; Windows: python.org installer + py launcher), requests 2.34.2; fake_model_server.py (stdlib); optional: Ollama 0.40.12 + qwen2.5:1.5b (Q4_K_M, 986 MB; CPU, or GPU via Metal on Apple silicon / CUDA, ROCm or Vulkan on Windows)
overview: An agent is a loop: call the model, run any requested tools, append results, repeat until it answers or the budget runs out.

glossary.meaning: Repeated model calls where tool results feed the next call.
max_steps hard limit so a confused model cannot loop forever (or burn cost).

concepts: The loop, the budget and the tool allow-list are plain code you control.
Tool errors go back to the model as text instead of crashing the loop.
Risky tools require an approval callback that defaults to deny.
inRealSystems: Ollama's docs show the same while-loop; LangGraph draws it as LLM node + tool node + conditional edge.
useWhen: When steps depend on intermediate results; a fixed sequence when they are known in advance.
